short: Ports a 2023 ECoG recipe (text-to-speech HuBERT units, CTC) to EMG; phoneme guidance (M02) and covariance input (M06) are standard. Table 6 mixes listener and decoder scoring, so it ranks no route.
position: The paper [@gowda2025emg2speech] ports to surface EMG the ECoG synthesis pipeline it says it adopts [@metzger2023]: HuBERT units from text-to-speech audio, learned with CTC (§5.3) and voiced by a pretrained Tacotron "vocoder" (§2). Its own changes, an auxiliary phoneme CTC head with a consistency loss (M02) and a covariance input from the same group's earlier work (M06) [@gowda2025], are standard; auxiliary phoneme losses for EMG voicing date from 2021 [@gaddy2021improved]. The strongest confound is the paper's Table 6: its text route reports 51.17% WER (decoder output) against 61.02% for direct synthesis (listener transcripts, 460 sentences, Appendix D.3), but the scoring differs and the text decoder was trained "on all 460 sentences" (Appendix D.4), so the table ranks neither route, and the "more fluid, natural interaction" claimed for direct synthesis is untested. Listener WERs of 62.55% (healthy, vocalized) and 50.82% (one ALS participant, silent) stay far above 11.89% to 12.2% for silent EMG on the Gaddy benchmark [@lee2026gets; @benster2024crossmodal], with other corpora and scoring.
